name: GenPept-Curated-2025
description: Abstract Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising therapeutic candidates against rising antimicrobial resistance, yet progress in AMP prediction is hampered by the lack of benchmark datasets that address homology leakage, negative set reliability, and distributional diversity. Existing AMP databases, designed as biological repositories, do not enforce the controlled partitioning required for rigorous machine learning evaluation.
